clue.text: One noted for stubborn tenacity makes target with almighty backing

parts.note: the bull is the centre of a dartboard or shooting target

indicators.note: backing means the word for the Almighty is read in reverse

parts.note: the Almighty is God

explanation.surface: Someone famously stubborn sets a goal with divine support behind them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reads the Almighty's name backwards, giving the animal; 'makes' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The breed is proverbial for refusing to let go, hence the 'bulldog spirit' of dogged persistence.

clue.text: Kiss before drug, keeling over in roadside shelter?

parts.note: buss is an old word for a kiss

indicators.note: keeling over means toppling, so the word for the drug is turned upside down in this down entry

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A kiss and then a drug, with someone collapsing at the roadside.
explanation.definitionFit: The question mark admits the shelter at a stopping point is a bus shelter, a waiting spot beside a road.

clue.text: Scottish pop diva's footballer being dragged along on new song

parts.note: Lulu is the Glasgow-born singer of Shout, and the possessive gives the final S
a back is a defending footballer, such as a full-back
something being dragged along behind is in tow

explanation.surface: A Scottish singer's footballer boyfriend is pulled along on a new single.
explanation.walkthrough: Lulu is a Scottish pop singer famous since the 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the title of a 1930s popular song, recorded by Fats Waller among others.

clue.text: Yorkshire town established by duke, eccentric ancestor

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters of ancestor are rearranged

explanation.surface: A northern town was founded by a duke with a peculiar forebear.
explanation.walkthrough: Doncaster is a town in South Yorkshire, England, famous for its racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a South Yorkshire town, home of the St Leger horse race.

clue.text: Visitor figured in conversation

indicators.note: in conversation signals a word as spoken rather than written

parts.note: to figure is to guess or reckon, so figured is guessed

explanation.surface: A visitor appeared or was talked about in a chat.
explanation.definitionFit: A person invited to stay or eat at someone's home is a visitor there.

clue.text: Granted time for deliberation

parts.note: 'granted' and 'though' both concede a point (granted, it's late; though it's late)

explanation.surface: Someone has been given time to consider a matter carefully.
explanation.definitionFit: Careful thinking or consideration is synonymous with deliberation.

clue.text: Airman up for trial?

parts.note: up for trial suggests a pilot facing a court, but it means one flying to try out new aircraft

explanation.surface: A flyer is in court facing charges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up for trial' suggests a defendant; 'up' is in the air, and the trial is of an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: This flyer takes new or modified aircraft up to evaluate their performance.

clue.text: Atmosphere in office, initially gloomy

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of office is taken

parts.note: dour means stern or gloomy

explanation.surface: The mood in the workplace is gloomy at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A pervading quality or aura, as in 'an odour of scandal', is an atmosphere.

clue.text: Fail school subject — but be remembered

parts.note: to go down in an exam or subject is to fail it
history is taught as a subject at school

explanation.surface: A pupil flunks a subject, yet will be remembered for it.
explanation.walkthrough: Read cryptically, the phrase means fail an exam in history.
explanation.definitionFit: To be recorded by posterity for one's deeds is to be remembered.

clue.text: Climber needs to catch up on correct procedure, mostly

indicators.note: up means the word for catch is read upwards in this down entry, so backwards

parts.note: to net a fish is to catch it

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: the drill is the correct routine, as in 'you know the drill'

explanation.surface: A mountaineer has to brush up on proper practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns NET into TEN; 'mostly' cuts DRILL to DRIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendril is the slender coiling shoot by which a climbing plant clings.

clue.text: Frolicking inside college in outskirts of Swindon? Best say nothing

indicators.note: in signals the rearranged letters are placed within the outer letters of Swindon
the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters
frolicking suggests letters romping about, so the words inside and college are rearranged together

explanation.surface: Students larking about inside a college near Swindon are advised to keep quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' looks like a positional word but is part of what 'Frolicking' jumbles, along with 'college'; the 'in' that follows places the result between Swindon's outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb advises that keeping quiet is often the wisest course, matching the idea that saying nothing is best.

clue.text: Coats designed for an opera

indicators.note: designed means put together in a new pattern, so the letters of coats are rearranged

explanation.surface: Costumes are being made for an opera production.
explanation.definitionFit: Puccini's work about the singer Floria is one of the best-known operas in the repertoire.

clue.text: Of high quality, prize trophy goes west

indicators.note: goes west means travels leftwards, so the combined letters are read backwards in an across entry

parts.note: a prize is a reward
a pot is slang for a trophy or cup

explanation.surface: A first-class prize cup has gone missing, or died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes west' reverses REWARDPOT as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Something from the top drawer is the finest, of the highest class or standard.

clue.text: Applied, being sensible

definitions.meaning: applied as opposed to theoretical, as in hands-on rather than abstract
sensible in the sense of down-to-earth and realistic

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both put to real use rather than theoretical, and level-headed and realistic.

clue.text: Blaze under bridge, something one doesn't want to be caught in

definitions.text: something one doesn't want to be caught in

indicators.note: under places the word for blaze below the word for bridge in this down entry

parts.note: to bridge a gap is to cross it
a blaze is a fire

explanation.surface: A fire breaks out beneath a bridge, where nobody wants to be trapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Fire from two directions at once is a hazard nobody wants to be trapped in, literally or figuratively.

clue.text: Fish, first from babbling brook

indicators.note: first from means only the opening letter of babbling is taken

parts.note: a rill is a small stream or brook

explanation.surface: A fish is pulled first out of a burbling stream.
explanation.definitionFit: A flatfish related to the turbot, found in European waters.

clue.text: Damage that is seen after child runs off vessel used by cook

indicators.note: seen after places the earlier pieces behind the shortened word for child
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs, and off says it is removed

parts.note: bairn is a Scottish word for a child
to mar is to damage
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: Harm is evident once a youngster has fled, involving a kitchen pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs off' takes R from BAIRN, giving BAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A water bath, a pan of hot water in which another dish sits to cook gently.

clue.text: One who sells tins, rye and soda?

definitions.text: One who sells tins, rye and soda?

parts.words: One who sells tins, rye and soda?
parts.note: the list reads like a drinks or grocery order, but tin loaves, rye bread and soda bread are all breads

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper's stock appears to be canned goods, whisky and mixers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tins', 'rye' and 'soda' suggest cans and drinks; each is in fact a kind of loaf.
explanation.definitionFit: A tin loaf, rye bread and soda bread are all sold by someone who makes and sells bread.

clue.text: Attack doctor dividing committee

indicators.note: dividing means the doctor splits the committee word by sitting inside it

parts.note: a board is a governing committee
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A medic is causing a split in a committee and launching an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: To bombard is to attack with sustained shelling or a barrage.

clue.text: Dismissed in style? Say what you're thinking

parts.note: a batsman who is dismissed in cricket is out
with it is slang for fashionable or up to date

explanation.surface: Someone sacked in fashionable fashion is urged to speak their mind.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is an impatient demand that someone speak up and tell what they know.

clue.text: Pot if tense? Head of agency drank bubbly

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of agency
bubbly means fizzing and lively, so the letters of drank are stirred up

explanation.surface: An anxious agency boss knocked back champagne from a beer mug.
explanation.definitionFit: A large drinking mug for beer can be called a pot, as in a pot of ale.

clue.text: Aims often set out in this

definitions.text: Aims often set out in this

indicators.note: set out means arranged afresh, so the letters of aims often are rearranged

explanation.surface: A document in which goals are regularly laid out.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: 'set out' does double duty as anagram signal and as 'stated'.
explanation.definitionFit: A party's published declaration of policy is where its aims are set out.

clue.text: Fast naval force

definitions.meaning: fast in the sense of nimble and swift
a group of warships under one command

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both swift of foot and a navy's assembled ships.

clue.text: Admit academic robe's no good at university

indicators.note: no means the letter for good is taken away from the robe

parts.note: a gown is worn by academics
a student in residence at university is up

explanation.surface: A don confesses their gown is worthless at college.
explanation.definitionFit: To confess or acknowledge a fault is to admit it.

clue.text: Male, when working, is one who dresses stone

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: A man at work turns out to be a stoneworker.
explanation.definitionFit: A stonemason cuts and shapes, or dresses, building stone.

clue.text: Medical condition of an old king — a version inaccurately advanced

parts.note: Rex is Latin for king, as on coins

indicators.note: inaccurately means the letters of a version are not in their correct order

parts.note: A is an abbreviation for advanced, as in A-level

explanation.surface: An elderly monarch's ailment is described in a garbled forward-looking account.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an eating disorder involving severe self-starvation, a recognised illness.

clue.text: A place to eat? Daughter and I clear end of table

parts.note: to clear a sum is to make it as profit after deductions, to nett it

indicators.note: end of means only the last letter of table is used

explanation.surface: A father and daughter clear the dishes from one end of the dining table.
explanation.definitionFit: A small dining area or alcove, often off a kitchen, where meals are taken.

clue.text: Greek character reportedly regarded as drunk

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the Greek letter is spoken, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
to eye something is to regard it, so regarded is eyed

explanation.surface: A Greek man is said to be viewed as intoxicated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' applies only to the Greek letter; EYED follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang adjective for very intoxicated, perhaps from the bleary look of the eyes.
